page: OVHcloud t1-le-45 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 8 dedicated physical cores from an Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 45.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.62 GB per core. For acceleration, the instance is equipped with a single NVIDIA Volta V100 GPU featuring 16 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 300 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear division between CPU and GPU capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is positioned in the lower tier, as shown by weak ratings in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, alongside slower single-threaded compression speeds. However, multi-core CPU execution and memory bandwidth fall into the average tier. The standout performance lies in GPU-driven tasks; LLM inference benchmarks for small (135M) and medium (7B) models achieve top-tier prompt processing and text generation speeds, though large (70B) model processing drops to average levels.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t1-le-45 offers a balanced entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by pairing dedicated Intel Xeon cores with a Volta-generation GPU and local NVMe storage. This resource density makes it highly suitable for machine learning inference, small-to-medium LLM deployments, data science tasks, and parallel processing workloads that benefit from GPU acceleration without requiring the latest-generation hardware.
description: OVHcloud t1-le-45 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server designed for workloads requiring dedicated parallel processing power. Built on the KVM hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated physical cores of an Intel Xeon Silver 4214 processor clocked at 3.0 GHz, paired with 45.0 GB of system memory. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA Volta V100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, complemented by 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. While single-core CPU benchmarks place this instance in the lower tier, its multi-core and memory bandwidth performance remain average. Crucially, the V100 GPU delivers top-tier performance for small and medium LLM inference tasks. This configuration represents a cost-effective option for machine learning inference, data science, and parallel computing workloads that require dedicated GPU resources without the premium cost of newer hardware generations.
